blocks.text: Sulfur is an essential nutrient for plant growth. When soils become depleted in sulfate, sulfur is restored by applying sulfur-containing N/P fertilisers or sulfur-coated fertilisers such as sulfur-coated urea; soil components and microbes convert elemental sulfur into soluble forms for plants. Gypsum (CaSO4.2H2O; printed 5H2O) is also used as a fertiliser.

blocks.prompt: Why can elemental sulfur be spread on a field even though plants take up sulfur only as sulfate?
blocks.explanation: Soil microbes and soil chemistry oxidise the elemental sulfur slowly to sulfate, so the sulfur-coated granules act as a slow-release source that keeps supplying sulfate as the crop needs it.

items: Sulfur is an essential plant nutrient; restored with S-containing N/P fertilisers, sulfur-coated urea (microbes oxidise S to sulfate) or gypsum.
